item.title: Qatar calls Iran’s claim ‘misleading’, denies capturing 3 pilots after March strike
item.description: Qatar denied Iran's claims about holding three captured military pilots. Iranian jets allegedly violated Qatari airspace during a March operation. Qatar stated it found remains of one pilot and attempted contact. Authorities defended their territory after receiving no response from the pilots. The denial comes amid regional efforts to ease tensions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why Hurricane Lala is a historic threat to Hawaii’s Big Island
item.description: Hurricane Lala approached Hawaii's Big Island as a Category 1 storm. Powerful winds and heavy rain brought dangerous surf and potential flooding. Over 40,000 utility customers across Hawaii lost electricity. Residents prepared for destructive winds, falling trees, and extended power outages. The storm's path raised concerns about mudslides and wildfires.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 19th-century ships accidentally brought mice to islands 30 miles off San Francisco
item.description: The Farallon Islands are grappling with an overwhelming invasion of house mice, significantly disturbing the delicate ecological system. These rodents threaten the survival of native wildlife, with burrowing owls preying on them and subsequently impacting the vulnerable Ashy storm-petrels. A new eradication initiative involves dropping rodenticide bait from helicopters, driving efforts to restore the natural balance of this unique ecosystem.

item.title: In 1987, a British naturalist became the first professional warden of a remote Seychelles island
item.description: In 1987, British naturalist Ian Bullock established Aride Island as a key conservation hub. His initiative led to the successful relocation of endangered Seychelles warblers the following year, significantly bolstering the species' numbers and preventing potential extinction. Today, their population thrives, and Bullock's innovative conservation methods are now standard practices in island ecosystem management.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 2023, Chris Pratt listed his Pacific Palisades mansion for $32 million; three years later...
item.description: After multiple price adjustments and relisting efforts, Chris Pratt and Katherine Schwarzenegger are once again offering their Pacific Palisades home for $19.99 million. Originally bought for $15.6 million in 2018, this marks their fifth try to sell the opulent estate, which boasts six bedroom suites along with ample outdoor living spaces, a true testament to luxury living in Los Angeles.

item.title: In 2011, Myanmar suspended a giant China-backed dam after public outrage; it now plans to...
item.description: Myanmar has announced plans to resume the Myitsone hydropower project, valued at $3.6 billion, which has been inactive for 14 years. This China-supported initiative aims to provide essential electricity to the nation. However, challenges regarding environmental degradation and potential displacement for local communities raise serious concerns. Additionally, fears of earthquakes add a layer of safety apprehension for populations living downstream.

item.title: Meet Jamie Bell, 18-year-old London teen who started selling old Lego at 13 and generated over...
item.description: Eighteen-year-old Jamie Bell has remarkably transformed his Lego reselling passion into JTB Collectables, a burgeoning enterprise generating upwards of four hundred thousand dollars annually. Specializing in bulk Lego lots and sought-after minifigures, he appeals to other collectors. As he prepares for university, Jamie aims to grow his business further, securing his financial footing and building savings for the years ahead.

item.title: Magnitude-5 earthquake strikes near Spain’s Granada, damages homes and cars
item.description: An early Saturday morning saw a magnitude-5 earthquake rattling near Granada, Spain. In the metropolitan region of Alhendín, homes and vehicles faced damage due to the tremors. Emergency teams worked tirelessly to rescue individuals trapped in compromised structures. Fortunately, authorities report no structural harm to the iconic Alhambra palace. Interestingly, this seismic event coincided with a more significant quake occurring in Indonesia.

item.title: In 1958, the US moved 25 caribou to an Alaska island as emergency food for military personnel
item.description: Following the closure of the military base, a herd of caribou was introduced to enhance food reserves, leading to a dramatic surge in their numbers. With no natural predators or hunting, their population exploded, causing significant overgrazing that harmed the island's delicate flora and soil. This unchecked growth prompted the caribou to migrate to Kagalaska Island, raising new ecological concerns that wildlife authorities now face in managing the situation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1923, wardens began protecting a 35-acre Texas island where last reddish egrets survived
item.description: Nestled in Texas, Green Island proudly hosts the largest Reddish Egret colony globally, evolving into a sanctuary after extensive hunting significantly depleted bird populations. The island's lush vegetation creates a rich tapestry of nesting sites, catering to diverse coastal bird species. Dedicated wardens vigilantly safeguard the island against predators, striving to uphold its sensitive ecosystem. Yet, the pressing challenge of climate change threatens the future of this essential bird sanctuary.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1975, Chantal Doecke was evacuated from Vietnam to Australia as a newborn; 49 years later...
item.description: Chantal Doecke, an Australian woman, uncovered a remarkable truth about her past through a DNA test: her twin brother, Glenn, has been living just a stone's throw away in Brisbane. Separated at birth during Operation Babylift, their emotional reunion unveils deep connections and reflections on the impact of their wartime evacuation. Doecke passionately pursues acknowledgment for the countless children shaped by such historical decisions.

item.title: Indian-American CEO who sacked 900 over Zoom gets fired himself
item.description: Indian-American entrepreneur Vishal Garg has been ousted as Better Home & Finance CEO. The company cited concerns about his judgment and credibility after significant losses. Garg's removal follows his controversial 2021 mass layoff of 900 employees. He is now seeking to regain his position and is offering to work for one dollar annually. Better's market value has significantly decreased since its pandemic-era peak.
item.dc:creator: Chidanand Rajghatta

item.title: US used dioxin-laden oil for dust control in a town with 2,000 residents, only to spend $33.1 million for their relocation in order to protect their lives
item.description: The residents of Times Beach faced a critical situation when dioxin contamination was discovered, leading to their permanent relocation. Originally, this toxic substance was used on dirt roads for dust control during the 1970s. A devastating flood in 1982 heightened the community's concerns about contamination. To address the issue, an incinerator was constructed to manage over 265,000 tons of polluted materials.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: By 2060, discarded solar panels could total to 402 million tonnes; recycling them could...
item.description: Discarded solar panels will create significant waste by 2060, posing environmental risks. Proper recycling can unlock nearly one trillion dollars in economic value from these materials. Middle-income countries, especially China, will become major sources of retired solar panels. A phased subsidy strategy can ensure fairer economic benefits between richer and poorer regions. Building recycling capacity now prepares for a growing waste stream and strengthens supply chains.
